Realistically, Jordan are the outsiders of Group J. Sharing a group with Argentina, Austria and Algeria makes progression a tall order. The honest expectation is that simply being competitive — avoiding heavy defeats and perhaps claiming a famous point or result — would represent success on debut.
[...]
The expanded 48-team format, which lets the best third-placed teams advance, offers a slim mathematical lifeline. But the primary goal is to compete with pride, gain experience, and make history simply by being there. A single win or draw would be a landmark moment for Jordanian football.
[...]
Sellami’s Jordan are pragmatic and defensively disciplined, a necessity given the calibre of their Group J opponents. Expect a compact, deep-lying block — likely a 4-5-1 or 5-4-1 — designed to frustrate stronger sides and stay organised without the ball. Their threat lies on the counter-attack, where the pace and creativity of Mousa Al-Taamari can punish opponents who overcommit. Set pieces and defensive solidity will be central to any positive result.

results.title: Germany World Cup Preview: 2026 Predictions, Odds
highlights:
Drawn into a highly favorable group alongside Curacao, Ivory Coast, and Ecuador, Germany enters the 2026 World Cup looking to erase the failures of consecutive group-stage exits and reestablish its status as an international powerhouse.
[...]
The underlying metrics from their qualification campaign highlight a team highly comfortable in possession. Germany averaged 66.7% possession and maintained a 90% passing accuracy, scoring 16 goals while conceding just three across six matches. Defensively, they recorded four clean sheets during that span. However, an early 2-0 loss to Slovakia exposed a vulnerability to clinical counter-attacks against a low block, a tactical puzzle they will need to solve in North America.
[...]
Adaptability remains their biggest question mark. While they can suffocate weaker opponents, their defensive line — anchored by Antonio Rüdiger and Jonathan Tah — lacks the proven, world-class depth of previous generations. Nagelsmann has brought in specialist coaches to focus on set-pieces and physical conditioning, aiming to find marginal gains to bridge the gap between their current 10th-place FIFA ranking and the absolute elite. The betting market views them as a dangerous dark horse rather than an outright favorite, presenting a fascinating dynamic for a nation historically viewed as a perennial contender.
[...]
Our predictive models suggest an incredibly high floor for this roster, giving them a 98.7% probability of advancing past the group stage. While they project as heavy favorites to win their group, the data indicates a steeper climb in the knockout rounds, with just a 20.7% chance to reach the semifinals.

## Germany World Cup Prediction
[...]
Germany, facing Curacao, Ivory Coast, and Ecuador, should comfortably navigate the opening phase. The data suggests a 65.4% probability of winning the group, and anything less than seven points would be a massive disappointment. With a 90% passing accuracy and an average of 2.67 goals per game during qualifiers, their offensive floor is extremely high against lower-tier opposition.
[...]
However, their defensive vulnerabilities against elite counter-attacking sides make a deep championship run difficult. A quarterfinal exit appears to be the most realistic outcome for a team still rebuilding its identity. From a betting perspective, value may lie in backing them to win their group, but fading them against top-tier favorites in the knockout stages.

results.title: Jordan 2026 World Cup Preview: Nothing Will Stop This North American Party

Drawn into a fierce group alongside reigning world champion Argentina, European regular Austria and African giant Algeria, extending its stay beyond the group stage appears near impossible for The Chivalrous Ones.

Olwan knows where the back of the net is, while star forward Musa Al-Taamari will be key to helping Jordan progress swiftly up the field.

## Current Form
[...]
Jordan believed it was making the perfect start to 2026 after going two goals ahead in its opening friendly with Costa Rica. However, it was forced to accept a point after conceding twice in the closing stages. Something to guard against this summer.
[...]

## What We Can Expect From Jordan Fans
[...]
There is unlikely to be many Jordan supporters traveling to North America, especially considering the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, and their absence will put a dampener on its debut World Cup.
[...]
Soccer is one of the country’s most cherished sports alongside basketball, however, and there is no lack of passion within an excited fan base. Jordan’s presence is growing on the world stage and positive performances have naturally drawn the interest of the general public.
[...]
Any Jordan supporters who make the trip will likely be donning white jerseys, the nation’s home kit color, while there will also be a smattering of red shirts alongside them—the color of every Jordan away jersey.
[...]
Little is expected of The Chivalrous Ones this summer, with a group stage exit looking incredibly likely, but that will not detract from celebrations. After all, how many times will Jordan be able to face the world champions at soccer’s most illustrious tournament?
[...]
The fact Jordan reached the final of the most recent Asian Cup has certainly helped lift confidence levels, but avoiding defeat in any of its three group stage games appears the mightiest of challenges.

Their approximate FIFA ranking around 70th places them below the established powers in Group J, but not in the category of pure ceremonial outsider. Their last major-cycle form points to a side that is difficult to break open: roughly 4 wins, 4 draws and 2 defeats across a recent competitive sample, with only 6 losses in 21 matches under the broader recent coaching cycle.
